text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-woman panel is not evidence of anything. Panels are often skewed by chance or by who happens to hold senior roles; mixed panels discriminate too, and single-sex panels usually don't. If you lead with it, you shift the subject from the decision to your motives, and you look like a man explaining his rejection by pointing at women's faces. That rarely ends well.

The genuinely odd thing is the silence. Two weeks with no written reasons is worth chasing — politely, in writing, to HR, citing their own policy.

Also consider: "broad regulatory experience" may be exactly what a head of risk modelling role needed. Credentials in statistics aren't automatically the deciding criterion.
